paper.title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners

repo.description: Official PyTorch MAE pre-training and fine-tuning.

annotation_metadata.review_scope: Repository revision, PyTorch import, and all annotated symbol locations checked against pinned source; existing claim text and labels preserved.
annotation_metadata.paper_evidence_note: Original PDF bytes have not been verified for this metadata review. Claim text is curated; existing section/page/character spans must not be treated as verified PDF quotations.

claims.text: MAE uses an asymmetric encoder-decoder where the encoder operates only on visible patches without mask tokens, and a lightweight decoder reconstructs from latent representation plus mask tokens.
Masking a high proportion of the input image, e.g., 75%, yields a nontrivial and meaningful self-supervisory task.
The MAE decoder has 8 blocks and a width of 512-d.
The MAE reconstruction target is pixel values for each masked patch, with MSE loss computed only on masked patches.
Using normalized pixel values (per-patch mean/std normalization) as reconstruction target improves representation quality.
claims.notes: Normalisation is implemented; the quality gain is an empirical result. Relabelled 2026-10-27 from PARTIALLY_VERIFIED: no paper/code mismatch, and PARTIALLY_VERIFIED requires one (phase-6-design.md §2.5).

claims.text: The MAE implementation uses random shuffling of tokens and removing the last portion based on masking ratio, requiring no specialized sparse operations.
MAE pre-training uses AdamW optimizer with base learning rate 1.5e-4, weight decay 0.05, batch size 4096, cosine decay schedule, and 40 warmup epochs.
claims.notes: --blr defaults to 1e-3, not 1.5e-4 (README launch command passes 1.5e-4). Per-GPU batch 64 is not a mismatch.

claims.text: The learning rate is scaled linearly with the batch size: lr = base_lr x batchsize / 256.
The learning rate follows a half-cycle cosine decay after a linear warmup.
